Question: Bernardo chooses a three-digit positive integer \(N\) and writes both its base-\(5\) and base-\(6\) representations on a blackboard. Later LeRoy sees the two numbers Bernardo has written. Treating the two numbers as base-\(10\) integers, he adds them to obtain an integer \(S.\) For example, if \(N = 749,\) Bernardo writes the numbers \(10{,}444\) and \(3{,}245,\) and LeRoy obtains the sum \(S = 13{,}689.\) For how many choices of \(N\) are the two rightmost digits of \(S,\) in order, the same as those of \(2N?\)
